papers.title: The Riemann theta function near soliton limit
papers.abstract: It has been known that (the square of) Jacobi elliptic function can be expressed by an infinite sum of single solitons of $\sech^2$ shape. In this paper, we show that there exists a similar structure for higher genus cases. It turns out that this is just a consequence of the quasi-periodicity of the Riemann $\theta$-function. More precisely, we show that the second derivative of $\log \theta$ with the \emph{real} Riemann $\theta$-function of genus $g$ near soliton limit can be well approximated by the \emph{sum} of \emph{real} and \emph{regular} $g$-soliton solutions of Hirota-type in $g$-dimensional real space $\R^g$. This leads to a tessellation of $\R^g$, whose tile is an oblique prism divided into $2^g$ sections by hyper-planes of dominant exponents in the theta function. We apply the results to study quasi-periodic solutions to the KdV and KP equations. We construct the quasi-periodic solutions using the Schottky group, which uniformizes the corresponding Riemann surfaces. We also discuss solitons on quasi-periodic background by pinching some of the homological cycles

papers.title: Odd-even dichotomy in the waveforms of modified Emden oscillators of arbitrary integer power
papers.abstract: Closed-form waveforms of the modified Emden oscillators $\ddot x+(q+2)kx^q\dot x+k^2x^{2q+1}+\omega^2x=0$ of arbitrary natural power $q$, and of their damped $c$-deformed versions, are obtained through a generalized commutative factorization that reduces them to Bernoulli equations. We show that commutative factorizations of Li\'enard equations are gauge-conjugated forms of the nonlocal linearizing transformation of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Kundu and Lakshmanan, the factorization constant being half the difference of the roots of the associated linear oscillator. These oscillators display an odd--even dichotomy: for odd $q$ they are isochronous, with period $2\pi/\omega$ independent of the amplitude, within an explicitly bounded range of the integration constant, while for even $q$ the oscillations decay algebraically, as $t^{-1/q}$. The dichotomy is confirmed by an elliptic polar representation, in which the phase rotates uniformly for every $q$, and, for even $q$, by the Bendixson--Dulac criterion applied to the divergence of the vector field. We present a dissipative Lagrangian of Lurie--Rayleigh type and, for $q=1$, an autonomous Sundman linearization that yields a rational first integral, a Jacobi last multiplier and a non-dissipative Lagrangian; for every $q$, $\omega^2x^2+(\dot x+kx^{q+1})^2$ is a Darboux polynomial providing a global Jacobi last multiplier. Explicit waveforms and phase portraits are given for $q=1,\dots,4$, with and without damping, and a recent application to magnon dynamics in the magnetic semiconductor CrSBr is discussed.

papers.title: Lax equations for relativistic ${\rm GL}(NM,{\mathbb C})$ Gaudin models on elliptic curve
papers.abstract: We describe the most general ${\rm GL}_{NM}$ classical elliptic finite-dimensional integrable system, which Lax matrix has $n$ simple poles on elliptic curve. For $M=1$ it reproduces the classical inhomogeneous spin chain, for $N=1$ it is the Gaudin type (multispin) extension of the spin Ruijsenaars-Schneider model, and for $n=1$ the model of $M$ interacting relativistic ${\rm GL}_N$ tops emerges in some particular case. In this way we present a classification for relativistic Gaudin models on ${\rm GL}$-bundles over elliptic curve. As a by-product we describe the inhomogeneous Ruijsenaars chain. We show that this model can be considered as a particular case of multispin Ruijsenaars-Schneider model when residues of the Lax matrix are of rank one. An explicit parametrization of the classical spin variables through the canonical variables is obtained for this model. Finally, the most general ${\rm GL}_{NM}$ model is also described through $R$-matrices satisfying associative Yang-Baxter equation. This description provides the trigonometric and rational analogues of ${\rm GL}_{NM}$ models.

papers.title: Generating integrable systems from an autonomous ordinary differential equation
papers.abstract: The freedom to realise special-function dynamics within integrable Kummer-type Hamiltonian systems remains underexplored. We investigate this freedom through examples constructed from prescribed autonomous scalar equations, using the established reduction and mode-reconstruction framework. A local holomorphic equation $\rho^\prime = f(\rho)$ determines a family of canonical Hamiltonians on a selected energy level, subject to regularity and compatible branch choices. We introduce the category of log-augmented polynomial systems, whose polynomial mode equations retain logarithmic terms in their scalar reductions, and illustrate it with examples including the Lotka-Volterra model and a parity-time-symmetric dimer. For rational generating equations, we prove a correspondence with extended Lambert-W-type inverse laws and establish elementary evaluation of rational reconstruction quadratures, giving local solvability results for the associated coupled systems. Further constructions use inverse incomplete beta and inverse spherical Bessel functions and the modular $\lambda$ function. The modular example has explicit theta-constant mode solutions and a direct map to the Darboux-Halphen system.

papers.title: Lax representations for the Navier--Stokes equations
papers.abstract: We construct a family of Lax representations for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in vorticity form. The key idea is to introduce an auxiliary vector field, termed the \emph{vorticity-diffusion potential}, which recasts the viscous Laplacian diffusion term as a Lie-bracket advection term. On solutions of the defining equation for this potential, the viscous vorticity equation takes the form of a pure Lie-transport equation along a modified divergence-free velocity field, while the defining constraint itself is encoded as the curl-free compatibility condition for an auxiliary scalar potential. We further show that the reduction of this three-dimensional system to two spatial dimensions yields a Lax representation for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes vorticity equation, which we generalize to a family parametrized by an arbitrary smooth function of one variable.

papers.title: On the Cauchy problem for the Tzitz\'{e}ica equation: Soliton resolution conjecture and asymptotic analysis
papers.abstract: We prove the soliton resolution conjecture for the Tzitz\'eica equation, which is an important integrable model arising in affine differential geometry and characterizing proper affine spheres. Recently, Huang, Wang and Zhu (Math. Ann. \textbf{395}, 18 (2026)) reported the long-time asymptotic result for the Tzitz\'eica equation with purely continuous spectrum. Inspired by their work, we carry out a full asymptotic analysis of the Tzitz\'eica equation. Compared with the previous work, by developing the $\bar{\partial}$-nonlinear steepest descent method, we reveal that the solutions of the Tzitz\'eica equation exhibits three different asymptotic regions depending on $\xi:=x/t$. For the region $\xi\in(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)$, where there are no stationary phase points, we rigorously prove that the solution satisfies $u(x,t)=O_\xi(t^{-1})$ for $\xi\ge1$ and $u(x,t)=2\pi i+O_\xi(t^{-1})$ for $\xi\le-1$. In the region $\xi\in(-1,1)$, the phase function $\theta(z)$ has two stationary phase points. The corresponding asymptotic approximations can be characterized with an $N$-soliton solution as well as an interaction term between soliton solutions and the dispersion term with a residual error of order $O(t^{-3/4+b_K})$ with $0\le b_K<1/4$. In the transition regions $\{(x,t):1-\varepsilon<|\xi|<1\}$, the corresponding asymptotic approximation can be characterized by the dispersion term with a residual error of order $O(t^{-3/4+b_\varepsilon})$ where $0\le b_\varepsilon<1/4$. Our results provide a rigorous analysis of the long-time asymptotic behavior of solutions of the Tzitz\'eica equation in different regions and confirm the soliton resolution conjecture for the Tzitz\'eica equation.

papers.title: Multi-pole extension for elliptic models of interacting integrable tops
papers.abstract: We review and give detailed description for ${\rm gl}_{NM}$ Gaudin models related to holomorphic vector bundles of rank $NM$ and degree $M$ over elliptic curve with $n$ punctures. Then we introduce their generalizations constructed by means of $R$-matrices satisfying the associative Yang-Baxter equation. A natural extension of the obtained models to the Schlesinger systems is given as well.

papers.title: The gauge action on semi-discrete Lax representations, its invariants, and Lax-Miura type constructions
papers.abstract: We introduce and study explicit invariants with respect to the action of (local) gauge transformations on the set of semi-discrete (differential-difference) matrix Lax representations (MLRs) for a given (1+1)-dimensional evolutionary differential-difference equation with any number of components. Using these invariants, we obtain the following general results: - Sufficient conditions for nonremovability of parameters in semi-discrete MLRs. (Nonremovability by means of gauge transformations.) - Necessary conditions for two semi-discrete MLRs to be gauge equivalent. Effective use of these results is demonstrated. We present the general theory and apply it to MLRs for equations of Volterra--Yamilov, Cherdantsev--Yamilov, Toda types and Miura-type modifications. Also, we present a comparison with results of S. Yu. Sakovich and M. Marvan on gauge invariants for (continuous) zero-curvature representations of partial differential equations. Furthermore, we demonstrate procedures for constructing Miura-type transformations (MTs) for discrete (partial difference) equations (on the two-dimensional integer lattice) by means of gauge simplifications of discrete matrix Lax pairs (DLPs) and reductions of auxiliary systems associated with DLPs. This allows us to construct new MTs for (non-evolutionary) 4-point and 6-point discrete equations from [D. Levi, R.I. Yamilov, J. Phys. A 2009], [S. Konstantinou-Rizos, A.V. Mikhailov, P. Xenitidis, J. Math. Phys. 2015].
